claim: C. elegans SET-9 and SET-26 are highly homologous paralogs that share redundant functions in germline development.
source: C. elegans SET-9 and SET-26 are highly homologous paralogs that share redundant functions in germline development, but SET-26 alone plays a key role in longevity and heat stress response.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing fertility defects in double mutants (Figure 2).

claim: SET-26 alone plays a key role in longevity and heat stress response.
source: C. elegans SET-9 and SET-26 are highly homologous paralogs that share redundant functions in germline development, but SET-26 alone plays a key role in longevity and heat stress response.
evidence: This claim is supported by lifespan and heat stress assay data showing that set-26 but not set-9 single mutants exhibit extended lifespan and increased heat resistance (Figure 1B, 1C).

claim: SET-26 is broadly expressed.
source: Whereas SET-26 is broadly expressed, SET-9 is only detectable in the germline, which likely accounts for their different biological roles.
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP knock-in experiments showing SET-26::GFP expression in all cells (Figure 3B).

claim: SET-9 is only detectable in the germline.
source: Whereas SET-26 is broadly expressed, SET-9 is only detectable in the germline, which likely accounts for their different biological roles.
evidence: This claim is supported by GFP knock-in experiments showing SET-9::GFP expression only in germline cells (Figure 3A).

claim: The differential expression patterns of SET-9 and SET-26 likely account for their different biological roles.
source: Whereas SET-26 is broadly expressed, SET-9 is only detectable in the germline, which likely accounts for their different biological roles.
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between expression patterns and phenotypic differences.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 bind to H3K4me3 with adjacent acetylation marks in vitro.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 bind to H3K4me3 with adjacent acetylation marks in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by histone peptide array data showing binding to H3K4me3 with adjacent acetylation (Figure 6B).

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 bind to H3K4me3 with adjacent acetylation marks in vivo.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 bind to H3K4me3 with adjacent acetylation marks in vitro and in vivo.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data showing genome-wide binding patterns of SET-9/26 concordant with H3K4me3 (Figure 6C-E).

claim: In the soma, SET-26 acts through DAF-16 to modulate longevity.
source: In the soma, SET-26 acts through DAF-16 to modulate longevity.
evidence: This claim is supported by transcriptomic analysis showing DAF-16-dependent gene expression changes in germlineless mutants (Figure 4).

claim: In the germline, SET-9 and SET-26 restrict H3K4me3 domains around SET-9 and SET-26 binding sites.
source: In the germline, SET-9 and SET-26 restrict H3K4me3 domains around SET-9 and SET-26 binding sites, and regulate the expression of specific target genes, with critical consequence on germline development.
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data showing expansion of H3K4me3 domains in set-9 set-26 double mutants (Figure 8C).

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 regulate the expression of specific target genes in the germline.
source: In the germline, SET-9 and SET-26 restrict H3K4me3 domains around SET-9 and SET-26 binding sites, and regulate the expression of specific target genes, with critical consequence on germline development.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data showing expression changes of germline-specific genes in set-9 set-26 double mutants (Figure 5).

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 are highly conserved.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 are highly conserved and our findings provide new insights into the functions of these H3K4me3 readers in germline development and longevity.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence comparison with homologs in other species mentioned in the Discussion.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 function as H3K4me3 readers.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 are highly conserved and our findings provide new insights into the functions of these H3K4me3 readers in germline development and longevity.
evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro binding assays and ChIP-seq data showing binding to H3K4me3 marked regions.

claim: Loss of the COMPASS complex results in a global decrease in H3K4me3 levels in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, loss of the COMPASS complex, which is critical for methylating histone H3 lysine 4, results in a global decrease in H3K4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) levels, and reduced brood size (Li and Kelly, 2011; Robert et al., 2014) and extended lifespan (Greer et al., 2010) phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of the COMPASS complex results in reduced brood size in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, loss of the COMPASS complex, which is critical for methylating histone H3 lysine 4, results in a global decrease in H3K4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) levels, and reduced brood size (Li and Kelly, 2011; Robert et al., 2014) and extended lifespan (Greer et al., 2010) phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Li and Kelly, 2011; Robert et al., 2014).

claim: Loss of the COMPASS complex results in extended lifespan in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, loss of the COMPASS complex, which is critical for methylating histone H3 lysine 4, results in a global decrease in H3K4 trimethylation (H3K4me3) levels, and reduced brood size (Li and Kelly, 2011; Robert et al., 2014) and extended lifespan (Greer et al., 2010) phenotypes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Greer et al., 2010).

claim: Deletion of spr-5 results in fertility defects in C. elegans.
source: Interestingly, deletion of spr-5 or rbr-2, both of which encode demethylases that erase methyl marks on H3K4, also results in fertility defects (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009) and altered lifespan (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009).

claim: Deletion of rbr-2 results in fertility defects in C. elegans.
source: Interestingly, deletion of spr-5 or rbr-2, both of which encode demethylases that erase methyl marks on H3K4, also results in fertility defects (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009) and altered lifespan (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009).

claim: Deletion of spr-5 results in altered lifespan in C. elegans.
source: Interestingly, deletion of spr-5 or rbr-2, both of which encode demethylases that erase methyl marks on H3K4, also results in fertility defects (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009) and altered lifespan (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).

claim: Deletion of rbr-2 results in altered lifespan in C. elegans.
source: Interestingly, deletion of spr-5 or rbr-2, both of which encode demethylases that erase methyl marks on H3K4, also results in fertility defects (Alvares et al., 2014; Katz et al., 2009) and altered lifespan (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Alvares et al., 2014; Greer et al., 2010).

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 share 96% sequence identity.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 share 96% sequence identity and both proteins contain highly conserved PHD and SET domains.
evidence: This is a factual statement about sequence analysis.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 both contain highly conserved PHD and SET domains.
source: SET-9 and SET-26 share 96% sequence identity and both proteins contain highly conserved PHD and SET domains.
evidence: This is based on domain analysis of the protein sequences.

claim: PHD domains are known to bind to specific histone modifications.
source: PHD domains are known to bind to specific histone modifications (Shi et al., 2007; 2006), suggesting that SET-9 and SET-26 could be recruited to chromatin via binding to specific histone marks.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies (Shi et al., 2007; 2006).

claim: The SET domain of SET-9 and SET-26 contains mutations in conserved residues thought to be key for methylating activities.
source: Interestingly, the SET domain of SET-9 and SET-26 contains mutations in conserved residues thought to be key for methylating activities (Ni et al., 2012), making it unclear whether SET-9 and SET-26 could be active enzymes.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Ni et al., 2012) and sequence analysis.

claim: The SET domain of SET-26 exhibits H3K9me3 activity in vitro.
source: Nevertheless, a recent study reported that the SET domain of SET-26 exhibits H3K9me3 activity in vitro (Greer et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Greer et al., 2014).

claim: The set-9(rw5) mutation causes a premature stop codon and is expected to produce a truncated SET-9 protein lacking the conserved PHD and SET domains.
source: The set-9 mutant we obtained carries a mutation that causes a premature stop codon and is expected to produce a truncated SET-9 protein lacking the conserved PHD and SET domains (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by the description of the mutation and Figure 1A showing the mutation location.

claim: The set-26 single mutant lived longer than wild-type worms.
source: Consistent with previous results, the set-26 single mutant lived longer than wild-type worms (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by lifespan assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The set-9(rw5) mutation did not alter lifespan in either wild-type or the set-26 mutant background.
source: Surprisingly, although SET-9 and SET-26 proteins share 97% identity in protein sequence, the set-9(rw5) mutation did not alter lifespan in either wild-type or the set-26 mutant background (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by lifespan assay data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 proteins share 97% identity in protein sequence.
source: Surprisingly, although SET-9 and SET-26 proteins share 97% identity in protein sequence, the set-9(rw5) mutation did not alter lifespan in either wild-type or the set-26 mutant background (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a factual statement about sequence analysis.

claim: set-26, but not set-9 single mutant, was more resistant to heat stress compared to wild-type worms.
source: Similar to the lifespan phenotype, set-26, but not set-9 single mutant, was more resistant to heat stress compared to wild-type worms (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by heat stress assay data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The progeny number produced by set-9 and set-26 single mutants was slightly smaller compared to that of wild-type worms.
source: We found that the progeny number produced by set-9 and set-26 single mutants was slightly smaller compared to that of wild-type worms (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by brood size assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The homozygous set-9 set-26 double mutant derived from heterozygous parents (F1) exhibited a mild brood size defect.
source: Interestingly, the homozygous set-9 set-26 double mutant derived from heterozygous parents (first generation, i.e. F1) also exhibited a mild brood size defect, and this defect became significantly more severe in the second and later generations (F2 to F6, Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by brood size assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The brood size defect in the set-9 set-26 double mutant became significantly more severe in the second and later generations (F2 to F6).
source: Interestingly, the homozygous set-9 set-26 double mutant derived from heterozygous parents (first generation, i.e. F1) also exhibited a mild brood size defect, and this defect became significantly more severe in the second and later generations (F2 to F6, Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by brood size assay data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The set-9 set-26 double mutant displayed a mortal germline phenotype.
source: We performed a classical mortal germline assay and found that the set-9 set-26 double mutant indeed displayed a mortal germline phenotype (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by mortal germline assay data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: set-9 set-26 double mutants derived from homozygous set-9 set-26 hermaphrodites crossed with heterozygous fathers exhibited a significantly more severe brood size defect compared to those from heterozygous hermaphrodites crossed with homozygous mutant fathers.
source: We found that set-9 set-26 double mutants derived from homozygous set-9 set-26 hermaphrodites crossed with heterozygous fathers exhibited a significantly more severe brood size defect compared to those from heterozygous hermaphrodites crossed with homozygous mutant fathers (Figure 2C).
evidence: This claim is supported by brood size assay data from crosses shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Heterozygous mothers, but not heterozygous fathers, helped to maintain better germline function in the progeny of set-9 set-26 double mutants.
source: In other words, heterozygous mothers, but not heterozygous fathers, helped to maintain better germline function in the progeny.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the crossing data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: For sterile set-9 set-26 double mutant worms, variable germline phenotypes were observed, including a very small mitotic region with no differentiated cells, and a small mitotic region with sperms only or a largely normal mitotic region with oocytes only.
source: For the double mutant worms that became sterile, we observed variable germline phenotypes, including a very small mitotic region with no differentiated cells, and a small mitotic region with sperms only or a largely normal mitotic region with oocytes only (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), suggesting problems with both the germline stem cells and their subsequent differentiation.
evidence: This claim is supported by DAPI staining images shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: For fertile set-9 set-26 double mutant worms, germlines with a smaller but stable number of mitotic cells were observed.
source: For the double mutant worms that remained fertile, we observed germlines with a smaller but stable number of mitotic cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by DAPI staining and cell counting data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: GFP-tagged SET-9 was only detected in germline cells of C. elegans.
source: Consistent with our previous report (Ni et al., 2012), we found that GFP-tagged SET-9 was only detected in germline cells of C. elegans (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy images shown in Figure 3A.

claim: GFP-tagged SET-26 was broadly expressed in both the somatic and germline cells.
source: In contrast, the GFP-tagged SET-26 was broadly expressed in both the somatic and germline cells (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by fluorescence microscopy images shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Expression of SET-9 and SET-26 was restricted to the nucleus.
source: As expected, expression of these two proteins was restricted to the nucleus, which is consistent with their possible roles in chromatin regulation.
evidence: This is based on observation from the GFP knock-in experiments shown in Figures 3A and 3B.

claim: RNAi knockdown of wdr-5.1 extended lifespan in both wild-type and rrf-1 mutant worms.
source: As expected, RNAi knockdown of wdr-5.1 extended lifespan in both wild-type and rrf-1 mutant worms.
evidence: This claim is supported by lifespan assay data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: set-9/–26 RNAi knockdown extended lifespan in wild-type but not in the rrf-1 mutant background.
source: In contrast, set-9/–26 RNAi knockdown extended lifespan in wild-type but not in the rrf-1 mutant background (Figure 3C and D), indicating that inactivation of set-26 (and set-9) in the germline is not sufficient for lifespan modulation.
evidence: This claim is supported by lifespan assay data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Inactivation of set-26 (and set-9) in the germline is not sufficient for lifespan modulation.
source: In contrast, set-9/–26 RNAi knockdown extended lifespan in wild-type but not in the rrf-1 mutant background (Figure 3C and D), indicating that inactivation of set-26 (and set-9) in the germline is not sufficient for lifespan modulation.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the RNAi experiments in rrf-1 mutants.

claim: 887 genes were up-regulated in response to set-26 loss in the soma.
source: We identified 887 up-regulated and 946 down-regulated genes in response to set-26 loss in the soma (Figure 4A), and gene ontology (GO) analyses indicated that these genes were over-represented in multiple functional groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), with 'collagen' stood out as the most highly enriched GO term.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis comparing glp-1; set-26 double mutant to glp-1 single mutant.

claim: 946 genes were down-regulated in response to set-26 loss in the soma.
source: We identified 887 up-regulated and 946 down-regulated genes in response to set-26 loss in the soma (Figure 4A), and gene ontology (GO) analyses indicated that these genes were over-represented in multiple functional groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), with 'collagen' stood out as the most highly enriched GO term.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis comparing glp-1; set-26 double mutant to glp-1 single mutant.

claim: 'Collagen' was the most highly enriched GO term among genes with expression change in response to set-26 loss in the soma.
source: We identified 887 up-regulated and 946 down-regulated genes in response to set-26 loss in the soma (Figure 4A), and gene ontology (GO) analyses indicated that these genes were over-represented in multiple functional groups (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), with 'collagen' stood out as the most highly enriched GO term.
evidence: This claim is supported by GO analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 162 genes were up-regulated in the set-9 single mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the set-9 single mutant.

claim: 334 genes were up-regulated in the set-26 single mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the set-26 single mutant.

claim: 1888 genes were up-regulated in the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.

claim: 545 genes were down-regulated in the set-9 single mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the set-9 single mutant.

claim: 534 genes were down-regulated in the set-26 single mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the set-26 single mutant.

claim: 1644 genes were down-regulated in the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.
source: We identified 162, 334, 1888 genes that were up-regulated, and 545, 534, 1644 genes that were down-regulated in the set-9, set-26, and F1 set-9 set-26 mutants respectively (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis of the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.

claim: There was a significant over-representation of germline-specific genes among the genes that exhibited up-regulated expression in the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.
source: Interestingly, we found a significant over-representation of germline-specific genes among the genes that exhibited up-regulated expression in the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant, but not the genes that exhibited down-regulated expression (Figure 5D).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with previously reported germline-specific gene lists shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Loss of SET-9 and SET-26 does not affect the global levels of H3K9me3 in the set-9 set-26 double mutants compared to wild-type worms at the L4 stage.
source: Using Western blotting, we showed that the global levels of H3K9me3 were not detectably altered in the set-9 set-26 double mutants compared to wild-type worms at the L4 stage (Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The genome-wide H3K9me3 distribution between N2 and the F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant revealed highly similar patterns.
source: Inspection of the genome-wide H3K9me3 distribution between N2 and the F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant revealed highly similar patterns (Figure 6—figure supplement 1C, 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1C and 2A.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 are likely not the major enzymes required for H3K9me3 deposition in C. elegans.
source: Taken together the Western and ChIP-seq results, we concluded that SET-9 and SET-26 are likely not the major enzymes required for H3K9me3 deposition in C. elegans.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on Western blotting and ChIP-seq data.

claim: The PHD domain of SET-9 and SET-26 pulled down histones, in particular histone H3.
source: We found that the PHD domain of SET-9 and SET-26 pulled down histones, in particular histone H3 (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by GST pull-down assay data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The PHD domain of SET-9 and SET-26 specifically interacted with H3 peptides containing the K4me3 modification in combination with nearby acetylation (K9ac, K14ac and/or K18ac), but not H3K4me3 alone.
source: This assay revealed that the PHD domain of SET-9 and SET-26 specifically interacted with H3 peptides containing the K4me3 modification in combination with nearby acetylation (K9ac, K14ac and/or K18ac), but not H3K4me3 alone (Figure 6B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histone peptide array data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: 75% of the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions overlapped with the H3K4me3 peaks.
source: In this comparison, we found that 75% of the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions overlapped with the H3K4me3 peaks (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: 49% of the H3K4me3 peaks overlapped with the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions.
source: The reciprocal comparison revealed that 49% of the H3K4me3 peaks overlapped with the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The H3K4me3 peaks bound by SET-9 and SET-26 had higher levels of H3K4me3 marking on average.
source: We found that, on average, the H3K4me3 peaks bound by SET-9 and SET-26 had higher levels of H3K4me3 marking and their H3K4me3 marking was somewhat higher 5' to the summit (Figure 6—figure supplement 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by metagene plot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4A.

claim: The average summit of the SET-9 and SET-26 peaks was ~100–200 bp upstream of the H3K4me3 summit.
source: The results indicated that the average summit of the SET-9 and SET-26 peaks was ~100–200 bp upstream of the H3K4me3 summit (Figure 6—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by metagene plot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4B.

claim: The H3K4me3 signal intensity is positively correlated with that of SET-9 and SET-26.
source: The results showed that the H3K4me3 signal intensity is positively correlated with that of SET-9 and SET-26 (Figure 6—figure supplement 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by scatter plot analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 4C.

claim: 28% of the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions overlapped with the H3K9ac peaks.
source: In this comparison, we found that 28% of the SET-9 and SET-26 binding regions overlapped with the H3K9ac peaks (***p<0.001) (Figure 6—figure supplement 5A), and 98% of these shared peak regions were also marked by H3K4me3 (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq peak overlap analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 5A.

claim: A subtle but significant increase in H3K4me3 levels was observed in the F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant but not in the set-9 or set-26 single mutants using Western blotting.
source: We observed a subtle but significant increase in H3K4me3 levels in the F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant but not in the set-9 or set-26 single mutants using Western blotting (Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by Western blotting data shown in Figure 8A and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The increase in H3K4me3 levels was more prominent in dissected gonads of the set-9 set-26 double mutant.
source: This increase in H3K4me3 levels was more prominent in dissected gonads of the set-9 set-26 double mutant (Figure 8B).
evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence staining data shown in Figure 8B.

claim: A 'spreading' of H3K4me3 enriched regions around SET-9 and SET-26 binding sites was observed in worms lacking set-9 and set-26.
source: Inspection of the genome-wide H3K4me3 distribution in the three genotypes revealed a 'spreading' of H3K4me3 enriched regions around SET-9 and SET-26 binding sites in worms lacking set-9 and set-26 (Figure 8—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: For the H3K4me3 peaks bound by SET-9 and SET-26, statistically significant elevated levels of H3K4me3 were detected starting at around +500 and −1000 bp beyond the summit in the F1 and F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant compared to wild-type worms.
source: Statistically significant elevated levels of H3K4me3 were detected starting at around +500 and −1000 bp beyond the summit in the F1 and F3 set-9 set-26 double mutant compared to wild-type worms, where the 95% confidence intervals of H3K4me3 marking in the F1 and F3 set-9 set-26 mutants did not overlap with that in the wild-type worms (Figure 8C).
evidence: This claim is supported by metagene plot analysis shown in Figure 8C.

claim: For the H3K4me3 peaks that showed no detectable SET-9 and SET-26 binding, the average plot showed no significant 'spreading' of the H3K4me3 marking.
source: Interestingly, for the H3K4me3 peaks that showed no detectable SET-9 and SET-26 binding, the average plot showed no significant 'spreading' of the H3K4me3 marking (Figure 8D).
evidence: This claim is supported by metagene plot analysis shown in Figure 8D.

claim: No significant difference in the genome-wide patterns of H3K4me3 was observed in germlineless worms with or without SET-26, even in regions bound by SET-9 and SET-26.
source: Interestingly, we observed no significant difference in the genome-wide patterns of H3K4me3 in germlineless worms with or without SET-26, even in regions bound by SET-9 and SET-26 (Figure 8—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-seq analysis in germlineless mutants shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 3B.

claim: SET-9 and SET-26 binding likely normally help to restrict H3K4me3 marking specifically in the germline.
source: Rather, SET-9 and SET-26 binding likely normally help to restrict H3K4me3 marking specifically in the germline.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the differential effects observed in whole worms versus germlineless worms.

claim: For germline-specific genes bound by SET-9 and SET-26 that showed expression increase in F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant, their average H3K4me3 markings were highly upregulated in the F1 and F3 set-9 set-26 double mutants compared with wild-type worms.
source: We found that their average H3K4me3 markings were highly upregulated in the F1 and F3 set-9 set-26 double mutants compared with wild-type worms, and the elevation was noticeable at both the TSS and the TES and throughout the gene body (Figure 8—figure supplement 4B).
evidence: This claim is supported by metagene plot analysis shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 4B.

claim: For germline-specific genes, H3K4me3 expansion correlates well with RNA expression increase.
source: Therefore, it appeared that for the germline-specific genes, H3K4me3 expansion indeed correlates well with RNA expression increase.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 4C.

claim: Three components of the MLL complex (set-2, set-16 and wdr-5.1) significantly reduced the brood size of the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant when knocked down.
source: Whereas most of the RNAi treatment did not substantially affect the brood size of the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant, we found that three components of the MLL complex, which is well-established to deposit H3K4me3, including set-2, set-16 and wdr-5.1, significantly reduced the brood size of the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant when knocked down (Figure 9A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNAi screen data shown in Figure 9A.

claim: The F1 set-2; set-9 set-26 triple mutant had a drastically reduced brood size compared with the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant.
source: We again observed a synergistic effect, where the set-2(ok952) single mutant had a normal brood size as previously reported, but the F1 set-2; set-9 set-26 triple mutant had a drastically reduced brood size compared with the F1 set-9 set-26 double mutant (Figure 9B).
evidence: This claim is supported by brood size assay data shown in Figure 9B.

claim: set-9 and set-26 are duplicated genes that arose from gene duplication specifically in C. elegans.
source: Although set-9 and set-26 are highly conserved from worms to yeast to mammals, only one homolog in each of the other diverse species has been detected based on sequence and domain structure alignment (Rincon-Arano et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2017). Even the closely related Caenorhabditis species, such as C. briggsae, C. remanei, C. brenneri and C. japonica, only harbor one gene that is highly homologous to set-9 and set-26. These results suggested that set-9 and set-26 have arisen from gene duplication specifically in C. elegans.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence comparison with other species and supported by citations (Rincon-Arano et al., 2012; Zhang et al., 2017).

claim: Drosophila UpSET and mammalian SETD5 and MLL5 represent the likely homologs of SET-9 and SET-26.
source: Based on the similarity in sequence and domain structure, Drosophila UpSET and mammalian SETD5 and MLL5 represent the likely homologs of SET-9 and SET-26.
evidence: This claim is based on sequence and domain structure comparison.

claim: UpSET, SETD5 and MLL5 have not been found to harbor methylating activities.
